items.title: Every flat module over a domain is torsion free
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is a one-line implication, flat implies torsion free over a domain, and the proof is a short but genuinely two-step argument (statement lines 4913-4915, proof lines 4918-4922). The decisive move is to test flatness on the principal multiplication maps x : R to R, which are injective because R is a domain with x nonzero; flatness transports that injectivity to x : M to M, and that is exactly what forbids a nonzero element of M from being killed by a nonzero ring element (proof lines 4919-4921). It is not a formal consequence of the definition of flatness alone: the domain hypothesis is what makes multiplication by x injective on the ring, and it is used at that single point. The proof reaches the conclusion directly, with no remaining verification.
